title: Phrasal verbs
subtitle: get up, turn off, take off
summary: Understand phrasal verbs - a verb plus a small word like up, on or off - and use get up, get on / off, turn on / off / up / down, put on, go on / off and take off.

lesson.heading: What are phrasal verbs?
lesson.text: Phrasal verbs have two parts: a verb + a particle (a small word like **up**, **on**, **off** or **down**). The particle changes the meaning of the verb, so learn the two words together.

examples.text: I **got up** at 6.30 this morning. I'm tired now.
We should **get on** the bus. It's leaving in five minutes!
We **got off** the bus at the City Museum.

lesson.heading: turn on / off / up / down
lesson.text: You **turn on** or **turn off** a TV, a light, a radio or an oven. You **turn up** the sound to make it louder and you **turn down** the sound to make it quieter.

examples.text: He always **turns on** the TV at 9 o'clock to watch the news.
It's a sunny day. **Turn** the light **off**.
**Turn** the TV **up**. I can't hear it.

lesson.heading: go on / go off, put on, come on
lesson.text: **Go on** means continue. **Go off** means leave. You **put on** clothes, and you say **Come on!** when you want someone to hurry.

examples.text: Don't stop. **Go on** talking. It's very interesting.
Karen **went off** and forgot her handbag.
It's cold and windy outside. **Put** your coat **on**. / **Put on** your coat.

lesson.heading: One phrasal verb, different meanings
lesson.text: One phrasal verb can often have different meanings. Look at the rest of the sentence to see which meaning it is.

lesson.heading: The phrasal verbs in this unit
rows: enter / leave a bus or train
We got off the bus at the museum.
start / stop a machine or light
Turn off the TV and go to bed.
Turn the radio up. I can't hear it.
The plane took off at midnight.

lesson.text: Make a special page in your notebook for phrasal verbs and put them into groups - clothes, movement, machines.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with what the person says or does.
It's dark in here. Turn ___ the lights.
exercises.explanation: Turn on = start a light or a machine.

exercises.prompt: Our plane takes ___ at 6.25 and lands at 7.50.
exercises.explanation: A plane takes off = it leaves the ground.

exercises.prompt: Come ___! It's time to get up. You'll be late for school!
The children took ___ their school uniforms when they got home.
exercises.explanation: Take off clothes = stop wearing them.

exercises.prompt: It's time to turn ___ the TV and go to bed now.
Get ___ the bus at the train station, then walk about 100 metres and you'll see the theatre.
exercises.explanation: Get off a bus or train = leave it.

exercises.prompt: The students went ___ working until late at night.
When they got to the beach, he put ___ his swimming trunks and ran down to the sea.
exercises.explanation: Put on clothes = start wearing them.

exercises.prompt: The passengers are walking up the steps into the coach with their bags. What are they doing?
options: They are getting on the coach.
They are getting off the coach.
They are taking off the coach.
They are turning on the coach.
exercises.explanation: You get on a bus, a coach or a train when you enter it.

exercises.prompt: I refused the invitation to Maya's wedding. Which phrasal verb has the same meaning as refused?
exercises.explanation: Turn down an invitation or a job = refuse it.

exercises.prompt: Turn down has two meanings. Put each sentence in the right group.
categories: turn down = make it not so loud

items.text: Can you turn the music down? I'm working.
He turned down the job in Paris.

exercises.statement: Turn the TV down. I can't hear it.
exercises.explanation: Turn the TV up. I can't hear it. Turn up = make it louder.
